Central banks are coming into focus this week, with the European Central Bank due to announce its latest policy decision on Thursday - markets are widely expecting a 25 basis point rate hike, and are keen to see if what policymakers have to say about the potential policy path ahead.
That may well of course depend on how the energy price shock develops and how broad its impact on prices turns out to be. Brent crude futures
are up 1.4% at $97.58 a barrel after the U.S. and Iran extended strikes on vessels in the Gulf.

Back in Europe, political risks are creeping in with Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) surging into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday - yet another setback for conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

And finally in corporate news, traders are calling Novartis shares down around 5% whe when trading begins after its experimental drug pelacarsen did not cut the risk of major heart attacks and strokes in patients with a genetic risk factor in a late-stage trial.
